prompt:
Production GAME SPRITE PARTS only, transparent background. FOUR large readable glove/gauntlet hand cutouts in a strict 2 columns by 2 rows grid. Each isolated object completely within its equal cell, generous transparent gaps. This sheet will be cropped into separate sprites.
Match the reference heraldic 2D medieval game style: confident dark navy outline, broad flat light/shadow planes, muted material colors. No realism, no glossy 3D, no surface noise.
TOP LEFT: closed STEEL GAUNTLET gripping an imaginary vertical sword handle. Clear hand silhouette: broad rounded palm, ONE strongly visible bent thumb wrapping across the right side, chunky simple knuckle block (not separate skinny fingers), short flared wrist cuff at bottom. Steel grey with slate shadow and subdued ivory highlight, dark outline. No exposed skin, no weapon, no arm. Outline shape must read as a fist/hand rather than a circle.
TOP RIGHT: same silhouette and same view, but thick BROWN LEATHER glove, medium warm brown and dark brown shadow, small simple cuff. One visible thumb, broad palm/knuckle mass. No skin.
BOTTOM LEFT: STEEL gauntlet gripping an imaginary horizontal crossbow stock, knuckles on top, thumb visible on side, short cuff below and slightly toward left. Broad compact hand, not a blob or ball. No weapon.
BOTTOM RIGHT: matching BROWN LEATHER crossbow grip hand in exactly the same orientation.
Keep hands economical and rounded, like small board-game miniature attachments. Three or four big planes maximum, no tiny finger lines: one seam or one knuckle division is enough. Each has a visible short cuff and a thumb. No round discs or dots, no skin-tone circles, no arms or elbows, no weapons, no text, no labels, no characters, no panels, no ground or cast shadows. Four individual clearly silhouetted gloved hands on real alpha transparency. They must still read as hands after reduction to 20-26 pixels.
purpose: Final covered hand sprites replacing the rejected skin circles/fists.
